summary: This batch proves the Bike system has a double-entry-style voucher and ledger/reporting layer, while also carrying operational vehicle quantity and engine/chassis information into account ledgers.

observed: Journal Voucher supports multiple accounting rows and separate debit/credit totals.
Cheque No. and Pay Order fields are built into journal rows.
inferred: The form is a generic manual accounting adjustment/transfer mechanism.

observed: The rendered report identifies a dedicated cash account labelled CASH IN HAND (BIKE).
Debit, credit and running balance are reported.
Visible status codes include ADV/BOOK, C/P and C/S in the sample.
inferred: Status codes likely classify source transaction types; exact mappings require confirmation.
unknowns: Whether cash book is generated from one account only or configurable

observed: Ledger rows combine financial columns with engine/chassis and inventory in/out quantities.
The ledger can be filtered by account and date range.
PDF and spreadsheet outputs are available.
Debit, credit and balance totals are shown.
inferred: The legacy ledger/reporting model blends party/account activity with operational vehicle/stock detail.
unknowns: Whether all account types show Eng/Ch/In/Out data
Account master relationship to Head form

cross_image_findings: The Bike application has a clear accounting backbone: JV, cash book, account ledger, debit/credit and running balances.
Accounting reports retain source-operation context through status/reference plus vehicle/quantity fields.
The dedicated CASH IN HAND (BIKE) label is strong evidence that Bike cash accounting was separated from other business activity.
preliminary_erpnext_relevance: Use ERPNext accounting ledgers as the canonical accounting layer rather than recreating a parallel debit/credit engine.
Vehicle-specific context should be linked to standard accounting source documents, not embedded into a replacement GL schema unless a verified gap demands it.
